children.title: Court Sets Aside HUD’s FY2025 Continuum of Care Funding Notices
children.description_short: Court Sets Aside HUD’s FY2025 Continuum of Care Funding Notices
children.description_medium: In June 2026, a federal district court in Rhode Island set aside HUD’s November and December 2025 Continuum of Care notices after finding that their funding conditions violated the Administrative Procedure Act. California’s attorney general said the ruling prevented HUD from implementing those conditions. This was FY2025 notice litigation, separate from a later case over HUD’s FY2026 notice.
children.description_long: On June 29, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island set aside HUD’s November and December 2025 Continuum of Care notices. In a June 30 release, the California Department of Justice said the court found those notices violated the Administrative Procedure Act and barred HUD from implementing the challenged funding conditions. The release describes two successive notices: after a coalition sued over conditions in the November notice, HUD withdrew it and issued a December notice that retained the challenged conditions, leading plaintiffs to include both notices in the case. This child records that FY2025 litigation and its June ruling. It does not combine the case with later litigation over HUD’s FY2026 notice. The evidence used here does not establish that any particular grant was withheld, that people lost housing, or that the court found corruption or personal misconduct. The original claim that courts blocked the same overhaul three times in March, June and August 2026 is unsupported by the supplied record and is omitted. Later appeal status for the FY2025 ruling was not established in the sources reviewed.

children.title: Court Vacates HUD’s FY2026 Continuum of Care Funding Notice
children.description_short: Court Vacates HUD’s FY2026 Continuum of Care Funding Notice
children.description_medium: On August 7, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island vacated HUD’s FY2026 Continuum of Care notice after finding that HUD violated the Administrative Procedure Act in issuing it. HUD’s current page says the notice and its August 26 deadline were no longer in force. This was a separate case from the FY2025 notices set aside in June.
children.description_long: On August 7, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island set aside HUD’s FY2026 Continuum of Care Competition and Youth Homeless Demonstration Program funding notice. The California Department of Justice said the court found HUD violated the Administrative Procedure Act in issuing the notice. HUD’s current program page likewise says the order vacated the FY2026 notice and that its August 26 application deadline was no longer in force; HUD said it was evaluating the order and considering legal options. The FY2026 case concerned a different funding notice from the November and December FY2025 notices set aside in June. The evidence therefore supports two distinct court actions, not a third ruling against one unchanged funding overhaul. The sources do not establish housing losses caused by the notice or prove corruption, motive, or intentional illegality. The court’s same-day account said it did not reach the coalition’s other legal arguments after finding an APA violation. This card records the procedural judgment and marks consequences beyond the vacatur as unknown.

U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island

source_fact_map.quote: The U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island today set aside the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) Fiscal Year 2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for the Continuum of Care (CoC) Program in its entirety, preventing HUD from moving forward with the funding notice.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island today set aside the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) Fiscal Year 2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for the Continuum of Care (CoC) Program in its entirety, preventing HUD from moving forward with the funding notice. The Court found that HUD violated the Administrative Procedure Act in issuing the 2026 NOFO, so it did not need to consider the coalition’s other legal arguments.
